description: Demolition of existing garages and construction of 2 x 3 storey semi-detached dwellings on land to the rear of 124 Lordship Road.
decision_conditions:
The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

Detailed drawings/full particulars of the proposed development showing the matters set out below must be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority, in writing, before any work is commenced. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved which shall be implemented in full prior to the first occupation/use of the development and retained in perpetuity (if necessary). <p>All residential premises shall be designed in accordance with BS8233:2014 'Guidance on sound insulation and noise reduction for buildings' to attain the following noise levels:</p><ul><li>Resting (Living room): 35dB LAeq,16hrs (7am to 11pm)</li><li>Dining (Dining room/area): 40dB LAeq,16hrs (7am to 11pm)</li><li>Sleeping / daytime resting (Bedroom): 35dB LAeq,16hrs (7am to 11pm) and 30dB LAeq,8hrs (11pm to 7am)</li></ul><p>A test shall be carried out prior to the discharge of this condition to show that the required internal noise levels have been met and the results submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To ensure that the future occupiers are afforded an acceptable standard recommended residential internal ambient noise levels.</p>

<p>Any plant shall be installed, together with any associated ancillary equipment, so as to prevent the transmission of noise and vibration into neighbouring premises. The rated noise level from all plant and ancillary equipment shall not increase the existing background noise level (10dB below) when measured 1m external from the nearest residential or noise sensitive premises. An assessment of the expected noise levels shall be carried out by a suitably qualified (IOA accredited) and experienced acoustic consultant, in accordance with BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 ‘Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound,’ and any mitigation measures necessary to achieve the above required noise levels shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing for approval.</p><p>The plant shall thereafter be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved details.</p><p>REASON: To protect acceptable local noise levels.</p>

<p>Environmental noise impact assessment shall be undertaken of the potential impact of noise from traffic, industry, sports venues, commercial premises and railway etc around the application site should be considered for the design of the building fabric.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON:&nbsp;To protect acceptable local noise levels.</p>

<div style="">Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, full details and installation certificates by a MCS registered contractor must be submitted to and approved by the Local Authority to demonstrate at least the consented standards have been met, as set out in the hereby approved Energy Statement:<br>a) Solar PV panels annual electricity peak generation of 4.8 kWp<br>b) Installation certificate by MCS register installer<br>c) As built roof plan (1:50) showing PV array, maintenance and access paths, other plants and services, landscaping including fire breaks where applicable<br>d) Final Operation &amp; Maintenance manual including fire risk assessment where applicable<br><br>For completeness, a summary statement highlighting changes supported by detailed justification and assessing their impact between the approved and the revised strategies where applicable should be provided.<br><br>Where compliance is not met, a remedial plan and associated cost plan must be prepared and submitted to the Local Authority for approval detailing the necessary measures to meet or improve upon the ‘as designed’ performance. Shortfalls may attract an additional financial contribution to the carbon offset fund.<br><br>The development hereby approved shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thereby approved.<br></div><div style=""><br></div><div style="">REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and supporting net zero development in accordance with LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan and Section 14 of the National Planning Policy Framework.</div>

<div style="">Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, full details including as built ASHP system (or any other related fixed plant adopted) specification and supporting drawings and installation certificates by a MCS registered contractor must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority:<br>a) Minimum Heat pump Coefficient of Performance<br>b) Minimum Heat pump Seasonal Coefficient of Performance<br>c) Details of location of the condenser units from the heat pump systems and any noise solutions to mitigate the impact for nearby sensitive receptors<br></div><div style=""><br></div><div style="">For completeness, a summary statement highlighting changes supported by detailed justification and assessing their impact between the approved and the revised strategies where applicable should be provided.<br><br>Where compliance is not met, a remedial plan and associated cost plan must be prepared and submitted to the Local Authority for approval detailing the necessary measures to meet or improve upon the ‘as designed’ performance. Shortfalls may attract an additional financial contribution to the carbon offset fund.<br><br>The development hereby approved shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thereby approved.</div><div style=""><br></div><div style=""><div style="">REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and supporting net zero development in accordance with LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan and Section 14 of the National Planning Policy Framework.<br></div><div><br></div></div>

<p><span data-sheets-root="1" style="">No development shall commence until full details of the proposed Construction Methodology, in the form of a Construction Statement, is submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Construction Statement shall include details of the following relevant measures:</span></p><p><span data-sheets-root="1" style=""></span></p><ul><li><span data-sheets-root="1">An introduction consisting of construction phase environmental management plan, definitions and abbreviations and project description and location;</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">A description of management responsibilities;</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">Measures to prevent the deposit of mud and debris on the public highway;</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">A description of the construction programme which identifies activities likely to cause high levels of noise or dust;</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">Site working hours and a named person for residents to contact;</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">Detailed Site logistics arrangements;</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">Details regarding parking, deliveries, and storage;</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">Details regarding dust and noise mitigation measures to be deployed including identification of sensitive receptors and ongoing monitoring;</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">A suitably qualified person shall develop a separate scheme of noise monitoring and management which shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority;</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">Details of the hours of works and other measures to mitigate the impact of construction on the amenity of the area and safety of the highway network; and</span></li><li><span data-sheets-root="1">Communication procedures with the Hackney Council and local community regarding key construction issues – newsletters, fliers etc.</span></li></ul><p>The construction shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the details and measures approved in the Construction Statement for the related phase unless the written consent of the Local Planning Authority is received for any variation.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: Development must not commence before this condition is discharged to avoid hazard and obstruction being caused to users of the public highway and to ensure minimal nuisance or disturbance is caused to the detriment of the amenities of adjoining occupiers and of the area generally and to avoid hazard and obstruction to the public highway.</p>

<div>Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, full details including as built ventilation system (or any other related fixed plant adopted) specification and supporting drawings and installation certificates by a suitable contractor must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority confirming the ventilation system has achieved or or improved upon as set out in the hereby approved Energy Statement:<br>a) Minimum MVRH efficiency<br>b) Details of summer by pass where applicable including provision and location across the development<br>c) Details of the peak lopping and cooling module where applicable including provision and location accross the development<br><br>For completeness, a summary statement highlighting changes supported by detailed justification and assessing their impact between the approved and the revised figures where applicable should be provided.<br><br>The development hereby approved shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thereby approved.<br><br>Where compliance is not met, a remedial plan and associated cost plan must be prepared and submitted to the Local Authority for approval detailing the necessary measures to meet the required level of performance. Shortfalls may attract an additional financial contribution to the carbon offset fund.<br></div><div><br></div><div>REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and supporting net zero development in accordance with LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan and Section 14 of the National Planning Policy Framework.</div>

<div style="">Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, air permeability certificates demonstrating that a maximum of 3.5 m3/(m2.h) at 50 Pa has been achieved must prepared by a suitable contractor must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority<br></div><div style=""><br></div><div style="">REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and supporting net zero development in accordance with LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan and Section 14 of the National Planning Policy Framework.</div>

<div style="">The applicant shall provide the Whole Life Cycle Assessment for review by the Local Planning Authority, the report shall include full details to demonstrate the design measures that have been explored to optimise the whole life cycle carbon of the hereby approved development.<br></div><div style=""><br></div><div style="">REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and supporting net zero development in accordance with LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan and Section 14 of the National Planning Policy Framework.</div>

<p>Prior to commencement of development, a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) shall be submitted to and approved, in writing, by the Local Planning Authority.<br style="">The HMMP must include as a minimum:<br style=""></p><ul style=""><li style="margin-left: 15px;">a non-technical summary;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the [HMMP];</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the planned habitat creation and enhancement works to create or improve habitat to achieve the biodiversity net gain in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">all landscaping in accordance with the scheme;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be carried out for a period of 30 years from the completion of development;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">such maintenance to include the replacement of any plants that die, or are severely damaged, seriously diseased, or removed;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">specific measurable targets linked to target habitat condition; and</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the monitoring methodology and frequency in respect of the created or enhanced habitat to be submitted to the local planning authority.</li></ul><p>The development shall not be undertaken otherwise than in full accordance with the details approved which shall be carried out within a period of twelve months from the date on which the development of the site commences or shall be carried out in the first planting (and seeding) season following completion of the development. Notice shall be given, in writing to the Local Planning Authority when the:<br style=""></p><ul style=""><li style="margin-left: 15px;">HMMP has been implemented; and</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">habitat creation and enhancement works as set out in the [HMMP] have been completed.</li></ul><p>Monitoring reports shall be submitted to the local planning authority in writing in accordance with the methodology and frequency specified in the approved HMMP.<br style=""><br style="">REASON: To ensure the development delivers a biodiversity net gain through both on site and off site delivery, in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Hackney’s Local Plan Policy LP47 and London Plan Policy G6.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Prior to commencement of development a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved, in writing, by the Local Planning Authority.<br style=""><br style="">The biodiversity gain plan must include as a minimum:</p><ul style=""><li style="margin-left: 15px;">information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the plan will set out how the biodiversity gain objective of at least 10% gain will be met;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">a completed metric tool assessment documenting pre- and post-development biodiversity values;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">details of on-site habitats, including steps taken to avoid, mitigate and compensate harm in line with the mitigation hierarchy;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">any biodiversity credits purchased for the development; and</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">any such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify.</li></ul><p>REASON: To ensure the development delivers a biodiversity net gain through both on site and off site delivery, in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Hackney’s Local Plan Policy LP47 and London Plan Policy G6.&nbsp;</p>
